desk.headline: Revenue up 17% to $2.25bn, just shy of estimates; adjusted EPS up 30% to $4.36, record $33.0bn backlog; sees high-teens growth in 2027

numbers.eps_basis: adjusted (non-GAAP) diluted; GAAP diluted EPS $3.70 vs $2.80

results: Revenue rose 17% to $2.25bn, a touch below the $2.26bn analysts expected; adjusted EPS climbed 30% to $4.36 (GAAP $3.70, up from $2.80).
Growth was led by ISTAR & electronic warfare (+32%, including high-power laser systems in Asia-Pacific) and Land & Armaments (+28%, munitions for Israel); Aerospace grew only 4%.
Margins kept widening: adjusted operating margin 10.8% vs 9.7%. A higher tax rate (11.6% vs 8.2%) under new global minimum-tax rules and a $27m US pension charge held back GAAP profit.
Backlog hit a record $33.0bn, with the quarter's increase coming mainly from Europe; about 35% is due to be delivered by the end of 2027.
Cash flow was strong: the CEO cited $276m of free cash flow, and nine-month operating cash flow nearly doubled to $862.5m. A $1.00 dividend was declared.

guidance.summary: Elbit expects high-teens revenue growth and further margin expansion in 2027 compared with 2026. It gave no specific numbers and no separate outlook for the rest of 2026.

points: Management said 2027 growth should be led by Land and ISTAR, with key products including PULS rocket artillery (mainly Europe), Iron Fist vehicle protection and high-power lasers.
Europe is driving new orders; US growth is coming mainly from border-protection sales, while Aerospace is held back by slower aircraft production rates.
Margin gains were put down to more profitable work in the backlog, operating leverage and laser and other programmes moving into production.
Capital spending is up about 30% over the past year to expand capacity; management said supply-chain problems have largely been overcome.
Management pointed to higher taxes from the global minimum-tax rules as a drag on net profit.
call.source: Call coverage: GuruFocus call highlights via Investing.com, 17 Nov 2026

watch: Whether revenue starts to keep pace with the $33.0bn backlog, as only about 35% is scheduled through 2027.
Margin progress and the effect of the higher tax rate on earnings.
Middle East ceasefire stability and new European contract wins.
